ei.title: Prior Knowledge as the X-Factor in Reading
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.

questions.passage: The importance of ①<u>what</u> a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension ②<u>tested</u>. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge ③<u>enabling</u> them to outscore readers with far better abilities. ④<u>Prior</u> knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①what=관계대명사(정상) ②tested=과거분사(정상) ③enabling→enabled 오류(본동사 필요) ④Prior=형용사(정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① what: 'The importance of what a reader brings to the page' — 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 brings의 목적어 역할. 정상
❌ ② tested: 'had their comprehension tested' — have+목적어+과거분사 사역구문. 정상
✅ ③ enabling: 'their prior knowledge enabling them to outscore' — 이 문장에 본동사가 없음. 현재분사 enabling은 본동사 역할 불가. 과거시제 enabled가 맞음 ←정답
❌ ④ Prior: 'Prior knowledge ... was the x-factor' — 형용사 Prior가 knowledge를 수식. 정상
det.tip: 문장에 본동사 필수: enabling(현재분사)은 본동사 불가 → enabled(과거시제)

Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to ④<u>outscore</u> readers with far better abilities. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①consisted=구성되었다(정상) ②were→was 오류(단수주어 group) ③scored=점수를 받았다(정상) ④outscore=능가하다(정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① consisted: 'This study consisted of two groups' — 주어 study(단수)에 과거시제 consisted. 정상
✅ ② were: 'The first group were made up of strong readers' — 주어 The first group은 단수이므로 was가 맞음. were는 수일치 오류 ←정답
❌ ③ scored: 'Guess which group scored higher' — 과거시제 scored. 정상
❌ ④ outscore: 'enabled them to outscore readers' — to 부정사 뒤 원형. 정상
det.tip: group = 단수 주어 → was made up of (were는 수일치 오류)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①asked=요청받은(정상) ②outscoring→to outscore 오류(enable+O+to V) ③Prior=사전의(정상) ④lack=부족(정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① asked: 'students who were asked to read' — 수동태 과거분사. were asked to V 정상
✅ ② outscoring: 'enabled them outscoring readers' — enable+목적어+to V가 맞음. 동명사 outscoring은 enable의 목적보어로 부적합. to outscore가 정답 ←정답
❌ ③ Prior: 'Prior knowledge ... was the x-factor' — 형용사가 명사 knowledge 수식. 정상
❌ ④ lack: 'the lack of prior knowledge' — 명사 lack이 관사 the 뒤에 정상
det.tip: enable + O + to V: enabled them to outscore (outscoring은 오류)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①brings=가져오다(정상) ②who=관계대명사(정상) ③was→were 오류(복수주어 readers) ④was=~이었다(정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① brings: 'what a reader brings to the page' — 단수 주어 a reader에 3인칭 단수 brings. 정상
❌ ② who: 'students who were asked' — 선행사 students(사람)에 관계대명사 who. 정상
✅ ③ was: 'Though the second group of readers was not strong readers' — 주어는 'the second group of readers'인데, 'were not strong readers'로 복수 술어가 필요. group of readers 구문에서 readers의 개별 특성을 서술하므로 were가 적합. was는 수일치 오류 ←정답
❌ ④ was: 'Prior knowledge ... was the x-factor' — 단수 주어 Prior knowledge에 was. 정상
det.tip: the second group of readers were not strong readers — group 뒤 of+복수명사에서 개별 속성 서술 시 복수 동사 사용

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is ①<u>highlighted</u> in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was ②<u>made</u> up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①highlighted=강조된(정상) ②made=만들어진(정상) ③with=~을 가지고(정상) ④lacking→lack 오류(명사 필요)
det.analysis:
❌ ① highlighted: 'is highlighted in a study' — 수동태 과거분사. 정상
❌ ② made: 'was made up of strong readers' — 수동태 be+p.p. 정상
❌ ③ with: 'came to the page with a knowledge deficit' — 전치사 with. 정상
✅ ④ lacking: 'the lacking of prior knowledge' — 관사 the 뒤에 명사가 필요. lack(명사)이 맞음. lacking(현재분사/동명사)은 'the lacking of'로 쓰이지 않음 ←정답
det.tip: the lack of = ~의 부족 (명사). the lacking of는 비문법적

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were ①<u>knowledgeable</u> about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to ②<u>underperform</u> readers with far better abilities. ③<u>Prior</u> knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the ④<u>x-factor</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①knowledgeable(해박한) ②underperform(저조한←outscore) ③Prior(사전의) ④x-factor(결정적 요인)
det.analysis:
❌ ① knowledgeable: 야구에 대해 '해박한' 독자 → 적절
✅ ② underperform: '저조한 성과를 내다'는 사전 지식 덕분에 '능가했다(outscore)'는 원문과 정반대 ←정답
❌ ③ Prior: '사전' 지식이 결정적 요인 → 적절
❌ ④ x-factor: '결정적 요인'이었다 → 적절
det.tip: outscore(능가하다) ↔ underperform(저조한 성과를 내다)

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is ①<u>highlighted</u> in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of ②<u>strong</u> readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not ③<u>enough</u> for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their ④<u>subsequent</u> knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①highlighted(강조된) ②strong(강한) ③enough(충분한) ④subsequent(이후의←prior)
det.analysis:
❌ ① highlighted: 연구에서 '강조된' → 적절
❌ ② strong: 독해력이 '강한' 독자 → 적절
❌ ③ enough: 독해 기술만으로 '충분하지 않았다' → 적절
✅ ④ subsequent: '이후의'는 '사전(prior)' 지식이라는 원문과 정반대. 독서 전에 이미 가지고 있던 지식이 핵심 ←정답
det.tip: prior(사전의/이전의) ↔ subsequent(이후의)

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study ①<u>consisted</u> of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew ②<u>much</u> about baseball. The second group was composed of struggling readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their ③<u>comprehension</u> tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not strong readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better ④<u>abilities</u>. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the x-factor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①consisted(구성되었다) ②much(많이←little) ③comprehension(이해력) ④abilities(능력)
det.analysis:
❌ ① consisted: '두 그룹으로 구성되었다' → 적절
✅ ② much: 야구에 대해 '많이' 아는 것은 '거의 모른다(little)'는 원문과 정반대. 첫 번째 그룹은 독해력은 강하지만 야구를 모르는 학생 ←정답
❌ ③ comprehension: '이해력' 테스트를 받았다 → 적절
❌ ④ abilities: '훨씬 뛰어난 능력'의 독자 → 적절
det.tip: little(거의 없는) ↔ much(많은)

questions.passage: The ①<u>importance</u> of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. The second group was composed of ②<u>struggling</u> readers who were knowledgeable about baseball. After reading the passage, students in each group had their comprehension tested. Guess which group scored higher? The struggling readers. Having strong reading skills was not enough for the students who came to the page with a knowledge deficit about the topic. Though the second group of readers were not ③<u>weak</u> readers, their prior knowledge enabled them to outscore readers with far better abilities. Prior knowledge, or, in the case of the good readers, the lack of prior knowledge, was the ④<u>x-factor</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①importance(중요성) ②struggling(어려움을 겪는) ③weak(약한←strong) ④x-factor(결정적 요인)
det.analysis:
❌ ① importance: 독자가 가져오는 것의 '중요성' → 적절
❌ ② struggling: '어려움을 겪는' 독자 → 적절
✅ ③ weak: '약한' 독자가 아니었지만은 원문 'not strong readers'와 표면적으로 유사하나, 원문에서 'were not strong readers'는 '강한 독자가 아니었다'이므로 이를 'were not weak readers(약한 독자가 아니었다)'로 바꾸면 의미가 정반대가 됨 ←정답
❌ ④ x-factor: 사전 지식이 '결정적 요인' → 적절
det.tip: were not strong readers(강한 독자가 아니었다) ≠ were not weak readers(약한 독자가 아니었다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 연구에서 ____되었다: 독자가 가져오는 것의 중요성
det.analysis:
❌ ① overlooked: '간과되었다'는 중요성이 강조된 맥락과 반대
❌ ② questioned: '의문시되었다'는 강조와 다른 의미
❌ ③ concealed: '숨겨졌다'는 강조와 반대
✅ ④ highlighted: '강조되었다'는 연구에서 중요성이 부각되었다는 원문과 일치 ←정답
det.tip: highlighted = 강조된/부각된

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. This study consisted of two groups of students who were asked to read a passage about baseball. The first group was made up of strong readers who knew little about baseball. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 강한 독해 기술만으로는 ____하지 않았다
det.analysis:
❌ ① excessive: '과도한'은 부족하다는 맥락과 다른 의미
❌ ② harmful: '해로운'은 독해 기술의 가치와 무관
❌ ③ relevant: '관련 있는'은 충분성의 문제가 아님
✅ ④ enough: '충분한'은 독해 기술만으로는 충분하지 않았다는 원문과 일치 ←정답
det.tip: not enough = 충분하지 않은

questions.passage: The importance of what a reader brings to the page is highlighted in a study discussed by Hirsch in The Knowledge Deficit. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우수한 독자의 경우, ____이 결정적 요인이었다
det.analysis:
✅ ① the lack of prior knowledge: '사전 지식의 부족'은 우수한 독자가 사전 지식이 없어서 불리했다는 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ② their strong reading skills: '강한 독해 기술'은 결정적 요인이 아님. 본문은 사전 지식이 결정적이라고 함
❌ ③ their natural talent: '타고난 재능'은 본문에 언급 없음
❌ ④ the passage about baseball: '야구 지문'은 도구일 뿐 결정적 요인이 아님
det.tip: the lack of prior knowledge = 사전 지식의 부족 (우수한 독자의 약점)

questions.stem: 첫 번째 그룹은 독해력은 강하지만 야구에 대해 거의 모르는 학생들이었다.

det.korean: 첫 번째 그룹: 독해력 강+야구 지식 부족?
det.analysis:

❌ F: 본문과 일치하므로 F는 오답
det.tip: strong readers + knew little about baseball = 독해력 강 + 야구 무지
